keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's Belgian Congo starts only in 1890): the infobox gives 2,345,409 km2 and the Berlin settlement gave Leopold's organization 'the balance: 2,344,000 km2', which is about the extent of the modern Congo (2.10 M km2 on the gazetteer's grid, which undercounts coasts and water). But in 1885 Msiri's Yeke kingdom (Katanga), Tippu Tip's Maniema, the Lunda heartland and the Luba empire were independent, so the shape begins as the Congo minus them (about 1.50 M km2 on the gazetteer's grid) and the ledger adds each as it falls. Within the shape the Free State held only the river stations; the rest is claim.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the Arab war (January 1894) and Katanga (1891) the whole Congo is held, plus the Lado Enclave leased in 1894 (the page names the enclave and gives no boundary; Central Equatoria is a proxy, confidence 1). The infobox total 2,345,409 km2 includes water (77,867 km2); this shape is 2.14 M km2 on the gazetteer's grid.

ledger.note: 1885 July: the Congo Free State is created. Infobox 'Established: 1 July 1885'; the body says Leopold announced the name on 29 May 1885 and that it 'officially replaced the Association's name on 1 August 1885'; the page: 'In November 1884, Otto von Bismarck convened a 14-nation conference' and 'In 1885, Leopold's efforts to establish Belgian influence in the Congo Basin were awarded'. The map shows the recognised territory minus the independent African states.

region.text: the part of the Lunda kingdom's 300,000 km2 extent inside the Congo

ledger.note: 1887 (bridge): the Congolese part of the Lunda heartland passes to the Free State. The Lunda page: 'At the start of the colonial era (1884), the heartland was divided among Portuguese Angola, the Congo Free State, and British North-Western Rhodesia'; its infobox ends the kingdom in 1887. The page does not date the Free State's occupation (confidence 1).

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1887 February 24: Tippu Tip accepts the governorship of the Stanley Falls District. 'In early 1887, Stanley arrived in Zanzibar and proposed that Tippu Tip be made governor of the Stanley Falls District'; 'on February 24, 1887, Tippu Tip accepted.' The Arab-Swahili domain of Maniema is drawn as a client until Sefu's attacks of 1892.
1889 (bridge): the Luba empire splits and 'later joined the Congo Free State'. The page does not date the accession; the empire's infobox ends in 1889 (confidence 1).

1891 December: the Stairs expedition takes Katanga. 'On December 14, 1891 the armed Stairs Expedition of the CFS arrived in Bunkeya with 400 troops and porters'; Msiri was killed on 20 December 1891 and the territory 'was taken over for the Congo Free State'. The British accepted the Free State's possession in the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 1894.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1892 March: Sefu bin Hamid attacks the Free State. 'In March and April 1892, Tippu Tip's son Sefu bin Hamid began attacking Congo Free State personnel in eastern Congo'; Tippu Tip had retired to Zanzibar in 1891 (Tippu Tip page).

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1892 November: open war in Maniema. 'Open warfare broke out in late November 1892, when Sefu set up a fort on the Lomami River.'

1894: the Lado Enclave is leased to Leopold. 'In 1894, King Leopold II signed a treaty with the United Kingdom' giving him the Lado Enclave; Chaltin won the Battle of Rejaf on 17 February 1897. The page gives no boundary; Central Equatoria is a stand-in (confidence 1). The British reclaimed the enclave in 1910.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1894 January: the last Arab-Swahili forts surrender.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1894 January: Maniema is under the Free State. 'The war ended in January 1894 with a victory of Leopold's Force Publique'; the page does not say the Free State annexed Maniema but describes no other ruler afterwards.

region.text: the whole Congo plus the Lado Enclave

ledger.note: 1908 November 15: Belgium annexes the Congo Free State. 'The parliament of Belgium annexed the Congo Free State and took over its administration on 15 November 1908.'

wars.name: Stairs Expedition to Katanga
wars.outcome: The Free State's Stairs Expedition reached Bunkeya on 14 December 1891 (Msiri page) and Msiri was killed on 20 December (Yeke infobox); Katanga passed to the Free State.

wars.name: Congo Arab war

zones.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

wars.outcome: Free State victory: Nyangwe fell on 4 March 1893, Kasongo on 22 April 1893, Sefu died on 20 October 1893 and the last forts surrendered in January 1894.

wars.name: Congo Free State against the Mahdists (Rejaf)
wars.outcome: Dhanis' column mutinied in February 1897 and Chaltin's force won the Battle of Rejaf on 17 February 1897; the page gives no territorial result.

certainty.note: Recognised on paper at Berlin; effective control was the river and the stations. The independent African states within are subtracted year by year.
The boundary treaties with Portugal, France and the United Kingdom (1885-1894) are not dated by the pages opened, so no frontier is drawn sharp.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the Free State before 1890, and its Belgian Congo row (1890-1962, af-08) covers 1890-1908 as well: af-08 should start Belgian Congo in 1908 or merge this dossier with it; the two are one state in different names only after 1908. The 1885 shape is the Berlin territory minus the four independent African polities that the pages show (Yeke Katanga, Tippu Tip's Maniema, the Lunda heartland, the Luba empire); the Kuba (infobox end 1884) and the Kongo lands are inside it. The paper claim vs the effective occupation is the main uncertainty: the pages do not say when the Free State occupied Kasai, Orientale, Equateur or Kivu, so no gain is dated for them. The boundary treaties (France, Portugal 1885-1891, UK 1894 Katanga, Germany) are not on the pages opened. The Lado Enclave is Central Equatoria as a stand-in. Counterpart needing a dossier: international-association-of-the-congo (1879-1885). Page budget (new state, 2-5): five pages (Free State, Arab war, Tippu Tip, Msiri, plus the Yeke, Lunda and Luba pages for the handovers).
